newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Egyptian sole candidate to head U.N. atomic body.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian sole candidate to head U.N. atomic body.

text.p: Egyptian Mohammed el-Baradei on Wednesday emerged as the sole candidate to become the new head of the world's nuclear watchdog agency, officials said.

The executive board of governors of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) backed Baradei's candidacy for the post of director-general of the United Nations body by 34 votes with one absention.
The only other contender for the post was former South Korean science minister Kun Mo Chung, who received no votes, officials said.
Diplomatic sources said Chung's candidacy was considered too sensitive given the agency's cool relations with communist North Korea.

The board of governors was expected on Thursday to recommend Baradei formally for the post. The recommendation has to be approved by the next IAEA general assembly in September, but this is largely a formality.

If appointed, Baradei will succeed Hans Blix of Sweden on December 1. Blix, IAEA director-general since 1981, has earned plaudits for his stewardship of the agency, one of the smallest and most cost-effective within the United Nations.
